source.title: A-bases with the minimum of additive permutations: Some results and open problems

evidence.quote: A sequence \(X=(x_ 1,...,x_ m)\) of relatively prime integers is called a basis of additive permutations, or A-basis, if there exists a permutation \(Y=(y_ 1,...,y_ m)\) of X such that the vector sum \(X+Y=(x_ 1+y_ 1,...,x_ m+y_ m)\) is again a permutation of X. In this case, Y is called an additive permutation of X. Let \(\psi\) (X) denote the number of additive permutations of an A-basis X. The authors calculate \(\psi\) (X) in various special cases, and review some of their previous results on this subject.
